title: Newton's laws in real life
examples: What is inertia, and how does it affect my movement?
Can you give another example of force equals mass times acceleration?
How is the action-reaction pair different from just pushing something?

explain.say: Today we explore Newton's laws in everyday life.

items: Newton's laws explain how things move.
They use concepts like force and mass.
We will look at three main laws today.

explain.say: First we look at inertia, which is an object's resistance to change.

draw.text: Inertia: Resistance to change in motion

explain.say: For example, when you are standing still, you must push to start moving.

draw.text: Still object needs force to move

explain.say: Next we learn force equals mass times acceleration. This is written as F equals m times a.
If you push a small toy car, it accelerates easily with a small force.
Finally we look at action and reaction pairs. These forces always happen in opposite pairs.

faq.q: Why do I lurch forward when a bus stops suddenly?
faq.a: This is due to inertia. Your body wants to keep moving forward, even when the bus stops quickly.
asks: Why do I feel like I'm thrown forward?

faq.q: Does the force I apply always cause an equal and opposite force?
faq.a: Yes, that is Newton's third law. For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
asks: Are action and reaction always equal?
How do I know if it's a pair?

faq.q: Does the object's weight change the force needed to accelerate it?
faq.a: The weight is related to mass, but acceleration depends on the mass itself, not just the weight.
asks: Is mass the same as weight?

faq.q: If I push a wall, why doesn't the wall move?
faq.a: The wall pushes back with an equal force, which is the reaction. The forces balance out, so there is no acceleration.
asks: Why does the wall push back?
What happens if the wall is bolted down?

faq.q: Is inertia only about moving things?
faq.a: No, inertia is about resisting any change in motion, whether you are still or moving.
asks: Can inertia happen when I'm still?
Does inertia only apply to big things?

facts: Inertia is the tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion.
The formula for force is Force equals mass times acceleration, or F equals m times a.
Action and reaction forces always act on different objects.
A larger mass means a greater inertia, requiring more force to change motion.

quiz.say: A student pushes a heavy box across the floor. If the box accelerates slowly, what is the relationship between the force and the mass?

options.show: The force equals the mass times the speed.
options.say: The force equals the mass times the speed.

options.show: The force must be large because the mass is large.
options.say: The force must be large because the mass is large.

options.show: The force must be small because it is on the floor.
options.say: The force must be small because it is on the floor.

options.show: The force does not matter if the box moves.
options.say: The force does not matter if the box moves.

quiz.why: Because the mass is large, according to F equals m times a, a larger force is needed to achieve any given acceleration.

wrong.0: This confuses acceleration with constant speed.
wrong.2: This confuses the surface with the force calculation.
wrong.3: The force is what causes the change in motion, or acceleration.

quiz.say: When a rocket blasts off, it pushes gas downwards. What is the reaction force?

options.show: The ground pushes the rocket up.
options.say: The ground pushes the rocket up.

options.show: The rocket pushes against the air.
options.say: The rocket pushes against the air.

options.show: There is no reaction force involved.
options.say: There is no reaction force involved.

options.show: The gas pushes the rocket upwards.
options.say: The gas pushes the rocket upwards.

quiz.why: The rocket pushes the gas down (action), and the gas pushes the rocket up (reaction).

wrong.0: The ground is not directly involved in the rocket's initial push.
wrong.1: While air resistance exists, the primary reaction is with the expelled gas.
wrong.2: Newton's third law states that forces always come in pairs.

quiz.say: A small ball and a large bowling ball are both at rest. Which object has more inertia?

options.show: The small ball, because it is easier to move.
options.say: The small ball, because it is easier to move.

options.show: They have the same inertia because they are both at rest.
options.say: They have the same inertia because they are both at rest.

options.show: It depends on the surface they are on.
options.say: It depends on the surface they are on.

quiz.why: Inertia is related to mass. The bowling ball has much more mass, so it has more inertia.

wrong.1: Ease of movement relates to the force applied, not the inertia itself.
wrong.2: Inertia depends on mass, not just the current state of motion.
wrong.3: The surface affects friction, but inertia is an intrinsic property of the object's mass.
